title: OnePot PURE Cell-Free System
protocol: Prepare the bacterial culture media and media supplements as described in Supplementary Table 1.
Sterilize the materials required, including pipette tips, 96 deep-well plates.
Transform the expression strains indicated with the corresponding expression vectors using the heat shock method.
Add purified plasmid to chemically competent bacteria and incubate on ice for 20-30 min.
Place the mixture at 42°C for 30 s (heat shock).
Place the mixture back on ice for 2 min after heat shock.
Pipette 20 μL of bacteria directly onto agar plates containing ampicillin.
Incubate the plates at 37°C overnight.
Store the plates at 4°C for up to 1 week.
Inoculate 3 mL of LB media containing AMP with a single colony of bacteria from agar plates.
Incubate at 37 °C while shaking at 260 rpm overnight.
Mix 250 μL of culture with 250 μL of 50% (v/v) glycerol.
Store the mixture at -80 °C.
Inoculate 300 μL of fresh LB media containing AMP with 1 µL of prepared glycerol stocks in a deep-well plate.
Seal the plate with a breathable membrane.
Incubate at 37 °C while shaking at 260 rpm overnight.
Inoculate 300 μL of fresh LB media containing AMP with 1 µL of overnight cultures.
Incubate at 37 °C while shaking at 260 rpm overnight.
After 2 hours, induce cells with 100 µM Isopropyl β-D-1-thiogalactopyranoside (IPTG).
Grow for an additional 3 hours.
Mix 10 μL of culture with 10 μL of 2x Laemmli buffer.
Heat the mixture to 95 °C for 10 minutes.
Spin samples for 1 minute using a table centrifuge.
Load 10 μL of supernatant on a PAGE gel.
Run the gel in Tris/Glycine/SDS buffer at 200 V for 30 minutes.
Rinse the gel well with deionized water.
Cover the gel with Coomassie protein stain.
Incubate the gel for 1 hour.
Destain the gel in water if necessary.
Mix the Sepharose resin well by vortexing.
Pipette the required amount of resin into an empty gravity flow column.
Wash the resin with 30 mL of deionized water.
Apply 10 mL of a 0.2 M EDTA and 0.5 M NaCl solution to the column.
Add 30 mL of a 0.5 M NaCl solution to the column.
Wash the column with 50 mL of deionized water.
Store the column in 20% (v/v) ethanol at 4°C or proceed with re-charging.
Wear protective equipment.
Wash the column with 30 mL of 0.5 M NaOH.
Wash the column with 30 mL of deionized water.
Wash the column with 30 mL of 0.1 M acetic acid.
Wash the column with 30 mL of deionized water.
Wash the column with 30 mL of 70% (v/v) ethanol.
Wash the column with 50 mL of deionized water.
Store the column in 20% (v/v) ethanol at 4°C or proceed with re-charging.
Add 10 mL of 0.1 M nickel sulfate solution to the column.
Wash the column with 50 mL of deionized water.
Store the column in 20% (v/v) ethanol at 4°C or continue with column equilibration.
Remove all traces of ethanol by washing the column with water if stored in ethanol between steps.
Prepare bacterial culture media and media supplements as described in Supplementary Table 1.
Sterilize required materials, including pipette tips, two 96 deep-well plates, and one 1 L baffled Erlenmeyer flask.
Prepare buffers and supplements as described in Supplementary Table 2.
Filter sterilize all buffers using bottle top filters (0.45 µm) and store them at 4°C.
Add 1 mM TCEP to all buffers right before use unless indicated otherwise.
Use 2 mL of sepharose resin for OnePot protein purification.
Prepare the column as described in section 1.4.
Combine 20 mL of LB media with 20 µL of AMP.
Add 300 μL of the media into each of 35 wells in a sterile 96, 1.3 mL deep-well plate.
Inoculate each well except for EF-Tu with its respective strain using a 96-well replicator.
Seal the plate with a breathable membrane.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C while shaking at 260 rpm overnight.
Transfer 500 mL of LB media and 500 µL of AMP into a sterile baffled flask.
Inoculate the OnePot PURE culture with 1675 μL of the EF-Tu culture from a 14 mL culture tube.
Add 55 μL of each culture from the deep-well plate to the OnePot PURE culture.
Measure the optical density of overnight cultures at 600 nm in a 96-well plate using a dilution of 10x.
Incubate the culture for 2 h at 37°C with shaking at 260 rpm until OD600 reaches 0.2-0.3.
Induce the culture with 500 μL of 0.1 mM IPTG and grow for an additional 3 hours.
Harvest cells by centrifugation at 4°C and 3220 x g for 10 minutes.
Store the cell pellet at -80°C until further use.
Thaw the cells and resuspend the cell pellet in 7.5 ml of buffer A using a serological pipette.
Lysate the cells with a probe sonicator using parameters: 4 x 20 s pulse on, 20 s pulse off, at 70% amplitude.
Keep the cells on ice during sonication.
Place the probe deep enough into the solution without touching the tube.
Let the foam settle, lower the probe deeper into the solution, and extend the sonication time if a large amount of foam is generated.
Remove the cell debris by centrifugation at 21130 x g for 20 min at 4°C immediately after sonication.
Add the supernatant to the equilibrated column.
Close the column from the top and make sure there is no leakage.
Incubate the column for 3 h at 4°C under rotation using a tube rotator.
Elute unbound components from the column with 25 mL of buffer A.
Wash the column with 25 mL of 25 mM imidazole buffer (23.95 mL of buffer A and 1.25 mL of buffer B).
Elute the proteins with 5 mL of 450 mM imidazole buffer (0.5 mL of buffer A and 4.5 mL of buffer B).
Dilute the eluate with 25 mL of HT buffer, keep the mixture on ice.
Add 15 mL to a 15 mL centrifugal filter and concentrate to a volume of 1.5 mL.
Add the remaining 15 mL to the filter with the concentrated solution and concentrate to 1.5 mL once more.
Add 10 mL of HT buffer to the concentrated sample and concentrate to 1 mL.
Add an equal amount of stock buffer B and store at -80°C until further use.
Measure the protein concentration using the Bradford assay.
Concentrate the sample with a 0.5 mL of 3 kDa cutoff centrifugal filter to 20 mg/mL.
Dilute the protein solution 25-fold or 50-fold before concentration measurements.
Perform an expression test at this stage with different concentrations of the protein solution.
Keep the total volume of the solution constant and pipette the OnePot protein solution, including stock buffer B, at five different ratios.
Verify the OnePot PURE protein composition using SDS-PAGE.
Dilute 2.5 μL of the sample with 7.5 μL of water.
Mix diluted sample with 10 μL of 2x Laemmli buffer.
Load 5 μL and 2.5 μL of samples to the gel.
Run the SDS-PAGE as specified.
Aliquot the protein solution into 50 μL aliquots after verifying expression and adjusting concentration.
Store the OnePot PURE protein solution at -80°C until further use.
Perform optical density measurements (OD600) of all cultures to check growth rates.
Conduct an additional expression test of the specific strain to verify protein expression.
Prepare and sterilize pipette tips, one 5 L Erlenmeyer flask, and one 100 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Pipette 5 mL of resin to a column and prepare the column as specified in section 1.4.
Inoculate 35 mL of LB media in a 100 mL Erlenmeyer flask for an overnight culture of E. coli RB1 strain.
Incubate the overnight culture at 37 °C while shaking at 260 rpm.
Add 2 L of LB media into a 5 L sterile flask and inoculate with 12 mL of the overnight culture.
Incubate for 3-4 hours at 37 °C while shaking at 260 rpm.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation for 10 minutes at 3220 x g and 4 °C.
Store the pellet at -80 °C until further use.
Equilibrate the column prepared in step 3.1.4 with 30 mL of lysis buffer.
Resuspend the pellet in 20 mL of lysis buffer using a serological pipette.
Lyse the cells with a probe sonicator on ice using parameters of 11 x 20 s pulse on, 20 s pulse off, and 70% amplitude.
Centrifuge the lysate for 20 min at 21130 x g at 4 °C to remove cell debris.
Load the supernatant onto columns and let it pass through.
Wash the column with 30 mL of lysis buffer (Wash 0).
Wash the column with 30 mL of 5 mM imidazole solution (29 mL lysis buffer, 1 mL elution buffer) (Wash 1).
Wash the column with 60 mL of 25 mM imidazole solution (50 mL lysis buffer, 10 mL elution buffer) (Wash 2).
Wash the column with 30 mL of 40 mM imidazole solution (22 mL lysis buffer, 8 mL elution buffer) (Wash 3).
Wash the column with 30 mL of 60 mM imidazole solution (18 mL lysis buffer, 12 mL elution buffer) (Wash 4).
Elute the ribosomes with 7.5 mL of elution buffer.
Keep eluted proteins on ice at all times.
Add 22 µL of β-mercaptoethanol to 45 mL of ribosome buffer in a fume hood, taking safety precautions.
Add the eluate to a 15 mL centrifugal filter and concentrate to 1 mL.
Add 15 mL of ribosome buffer to the concentrated sample and concentrate again to 1 mL.
Repeat the concentration step twice.
Store the final product at -80 °C until further use.
Determine the ribosome concentration by measuring the absorbance at 260 nM of a sample diluted 1:100 in ribosome buffer.
Adjust the ribosome concentration to achieve a final stock concentration of 3.45 µM.
To dilute or concentrate ribosomes, use ribosome buffer or centrifugation at 14000 x g in a 3 kDa 0.5 mL centrifugal filter at 4 °C.
Verify the ribosome composition using SDS-PAGE by diluting 2.5 μL of sample with 7.5 μL of water, mixing with 10 μL of 2x Laemmli buffer, and loading 5 μL and 2.5 μL of the samples onto the gel.
Prepare bacterial culture media and media supplements as described in Supplementary Table 1.
Sterilize pipette tips, 5 L Erlenmeyer flask, and 100 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Prepare and sterilize buffers and supplements as described in Supplementary Table 2 using bottle top filters (0.45 μm).
Filter sterilize all the buffers and store them at 4°C.
Inoculate 35 ml of LB media in a 100 mL Erlenmeyer flask for an overnight culture of the E. coli A19 strain.
Incubate the overnight culture at 37°C while shaking at 260 rpm.
Transfer 2 L of LB media into the 5 L sterile baffled flask and inoculate with 30 ml of the overnight culture.
Incubate for 3-4 hours at 37°C while shaking at 200 rpm.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation at 4000 x g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 25 ml of suspension buffer and store at -80°C until further use.
Thaw and lyse the cells using a 130-watt probe sonicator on ice with parameters of 12 x 20 s pulse on; 20 s pulse off, at 70% amplitude.
Remove cell debris by centrifugation at 20000 x g for 20 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and measure its volume.
Add an equal volume of suspension buffer to adjust the final concentration of ammonium sulfate to 1.5 M and mix well.
Remove precipitate by centrifugation at 20000 x g for 20 min at 4°C.
Filter the supernatant using a 0.45 µm polyethersulfone membrane syringe filter before FPLC purification.
Collect the filtrate in a 100 mL glass bottle and keep the supernatant at 4°C.
Set up the FPLC system for hydrophobic-interaction chromatography purification using a double Butyl column (2 x 5 mL).
Choose lines A1 and B1 for buffer C and buffer D, respectively, and line A2 as the sample line.
Apply a default flow rate of 4 mL/min for the FPLC system.
Perform a system pump wash in 20% (v/v) ethanol.
Manually set a flow rate of 0.2 mL/min and mount the column.
Execute a system pump wash with water.
Wash the column with 3 CV of water.
Place inlets A1 and A2 in buffer C and inlet B1 in buffer D without TCEP.
Execute a pump wash and equilibrate the column with 4 CV of buffer C.
Add TCEP to buffers C and D.
Prepare 15 mL tubes or clear round fraction collector tubes for collecting elution fractions.
Place the inlet A2 into the bottle with the filtered sample.
Load approximately 90% of the sample volume onto the column.
Dilute the sample with 20 mL of TCEP-containing buffer C and load 10 mL of the sample onto the column.
Repeat the dilution step at least twice and load as much sample onto the column as possible.
Wash with 3 CV of buffer C to remove unbound components.
Wash with 5 CV of 80% buffer C and 20% buffer D.
Apply 50% buffer C and 50% buffer D for elution, with a total volume of 5 CV.
Collect the eluted fraction in collector tubes.
Elute all strongly interacting contaminants using 100% buffer D with a total volume of 5 CV.
Analyze the absorption spectrum of the sample fraction at 260 or 280 nM.
Pool all sample fractions corresponding to the third peak for further processing.
Keep the eluted proteins on ice at all times.
Gently overlay the recovered fraction onto 15 mL of the cushion buffer in four polycarbonate ultracentrifugation tubes.
Add a maximum of 15 mL of the sample to 15 mL of the cushion buffer.
Balance the weight of the tube well.
Pellet the ribosomes by ultracentrifugation at 100000 x g at 4°C for 16 hours.
Place all inlets into water and execute a pump wash.
Wash the column with 2 CV of water.
Place the inlet into a 0.5 M NaOH solution, perform a pump wash.
Subsequently wash the column with 3 CV of NaOH.
Place the inlet into water, perform a pump wash.
Then wash the column in 2 CV of water.
Place the inlet to a 0.1 M acetic acid solution.
Perform a pump wash.
Wash the column with 3 CV of acetic acid solution.
Pump wash.
Wash the column with 2 CV of water.
Place all inlets into 20% (v/v) ethanol.
Execute a pump wash step.
Store the column in 20% (v/v) ethanol by washing it with 3 CV of a 20% (v/v) ethanol solution.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash each pellet with 0.5 mL of ice-cold ribosome buffer without disturbing the translucent pellet.
Repeat the wash step twice.
Resuspend each clear pellet in 100 μL of ribosome buffer on ice using a magnetic stir bar at the lowest possible speed.
Collect the resuspended ribosomes.
Wash the tubes with an additional 50 μL of ribosome buffer.
Determine the ribosome concentration by measuring the absorbance at 260 nM of the sample diluted at a ratio of 1:100 in ribosome buffer.
Implement a final stock concentration of 10 µM.
Dilute ribosomes with ribosome buffer or concentrate them further by centrifugation at 14000 x g in a 3 kDa centrifugal filter at 4 °C.
Perform ribosome titration as specified in section 5.2, Supplementary Table 7.
Verify the ribosome composition with SDS-PAGE as specified in section 1.3.3.
Dilute 2.5 µL of the sample with 7.5 µL of water.
Mix diluted sample with 10 µL of 2x Laemmli buffer.
Load 5 µL and 2.5 µL of the samples to the gel.
Weigh the exact amount of tyrosine required to obtain a final concentration of 3.25 mM directly into the tube for the amino acid solution.
Add the corresponding amounts of amino acid stock solutions and water as indicated in the Final volume to add [µL] column.
Vortex the solution well.
Store the completed amino acid solution at -80°C until further use.
Add 500 μL RNase and DNase-free water directly to the vial containing lyophilized tRNAs.
Mix well by gentle vortexing to dissolve tRNAs; limit pipetting to avoid introducing RNases.
Measure the pH of the solution using a pH strip to ensure neutrality.
Prepare stock solutions for remaining components listed in Supplementary Table 4.
Thaw all aqueous solutions mentioned in Supplementary Table 5 on ice.
Add calculated volumes of stock solutions and water as specified in Supplementary Table 5 to mix well using a vortex.
Keep the mixed solution on ice at all times after preparation.
Aliquot the energy solution at 50-100 μL per tube while keeping it on ice.
Store aliquoted energy solution at -80°C until further use.
Vortex the main stock frequently during aliquoting to prevent precipitation of components.
Set up a PCR reaction as recommended by the polymerase supplier.
Amplify the target gene (e.g., eGFP) as a linear template from a plasmid or genome using gene-specific primers (500 nM).
Check the amplicon on an agarose gel for correct size and purity.
Use amplified DNA as a template for subsequent extension steps.
Set up a reaction of at least 50 µL.
Run 10 PCR amplification cycles with extension primers (2.5 nM).
Immediately add final primers (500 nM) to the same reaction after amplification cycles.
Run 30 cycles to amplify the extended PCR product.
Purify DNA fragments using a DNA purification kit.
Elute purified DNA in nuclease-free water.
Check linear template on an agarose gel for correct size and purity.
Measure DNA concentration in ng/µL using an UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Remove required reagents from the freezer and thaw them on ice.
Fill in the concentration [ng/µL] and length [base pairs] of the DNA in the corresponding yellow cells in the spreadsheet.
Use 2-10 nM of DNA for the reaction.
Fill in the desired total reaction volume in µL.
Ensure precise volume ratios of components to maintain correct ion balance.
Minimize the number of freeze-thaw cycles and the time samples are stored on ice.
Pipette calculated amounts of water, DNA, and energy solution to one side of the PCR tube or corner of a well on the 384-well plate.
Add required amount of any additional reagent on the same side as other components.
Minimize number of samples per experiment to avoid sample evaporation and experimental start time bias.
Pipette calculated amounts of protein and ribosome solution to the opposite side of the PCR tube or corner of the 384-well plate.
Use master mixes whenever possible to reduce impact of pipetting errors.
Spin reaction components for a short time (30 s) to merge them.
Add 35 μL of liquid wax and seal the plate with a transparent sealant.
Incubate for a minimum of 3 hours at 37°C.
Measure fluorescence intensity at the required wavelength every 2 minutes on a plate-reader.
Incubate the sample with 0.16 µg/µL of RNase A for 30 min at 37 °C.
Visualize the protein expression by running SDS-PAGE as specified in section 1.3.3.
Wash the unstained gel gently in deionized water.
Image the gel on a fluorescent imager using an excitation wavelength of 488 nm.
Stain the gel using conventional Coomassie staining methods.
